definition: The mechanical construction of a holdable Roblox weapon/tool, distinct from attaching a prop to an already-posed rig in an animator: a modeled part (or union of parts) is renamed 'Handle' inside a `Tool` instance, given `CanCollide = false` (so it does not physically collide with other players while held/dropped) and `Massless = true` (so it does not affect the holding character's physics), and then a 'Tool Grip Editor' plugin is used to set exactly where and at what rotation the character's hand grips it — separately from the part's own modeled geometry/pivot.
purpose: Produce a `Tool` a Roblox character can actually equip, hold correctly-oriented in the hand, and swing or drop, with physically sensible collision/mass behaviour while held.
visible_effect: An unconfigured tool part either collides awkwardly with the world/other players while held, throws off the holding character's physics if not massless, or appears held at the wrong position/angle in the hand until the grip is explicitly set.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Not applicable — a functional/technical setup step, not a viewer-facing effect on its own (though a badly-gripped tool would visibly look wrong in the hand).
physical_interpretation: `CanCollide=false` and `Massless=true` are both explicit opt-outs from Roblox's default rigid-body physics for this part, chosen deliberately because a held weapon should behave as an extension of the character's own animated pose rather than as an independent physical object.
use_cases: any weapon or tool meant to be equipped, held, and swung/used by a Roblox character via the standard `Tool`/`Handle` mechanism
setting a specific, deliberate hand grip point and rotation distinct from the part's own default pivot, rather than accepting wherever the part happens to attach by default
non_use_cases: a prop attached to a rig purely for offline animation authoring in a tool like Moon Animator (see `easyweld_join_in_place_preserves_relative_transform`, W08-71) — that is a different mechanism (a weld in an animator) solving a different problem (authoring-time attachment) than an in-game equippable `Tool`

a part that should physically collide or carry real mass while held (an intentionally heavy, physics-interacting held object) — the defaults this entry describes are for the common case, not a universal rule
interactions: easyweld_join_in_place_preserves_relative_transform, weapon_attach_under_root_avoids_subframe_chain_desync (this batch and W05-43) — sibling weapon-attachment entries at a different LAYER: those are about attaching a prop within an ANIMATION (a weld, a parenting choice); this entry is about constructing the actual in-game HOLDABLE ITEM the animation will later be played on, a prerequisite step those entries assume already happened

attach_item (`weapon_attach_under_root_avoids_subframe_chain_desync`'s own cadence_representation question) — this entry's Grip mechanism is Roblox's own OWN native equivalent of an attach offset, worth reading alongside that still-open question about `attach_item`'s offset-preserving behaviour
cadence_representation: Out of Cadence's own animate-not-model scope as a CONSTRUCTION step (building a `Tool`/`Handle`/Grip from raw parts is rig-building, not animating an existing rig) — consistent with this same batch's verdict on the video 71 DIY face-plate rig-building. Worth recording anyway as a completeness note: if a future capability ever imports or targets a Roblox `Tool` specifically (rather than a plain rig), its `CanCollide`/`Massless`/`Grip` properties are real, load-bearing state a faithful round-trip would need to preserve, not just its `Handle` part's mesh/appearance.
control_surface: Not applicable — no tool-construction capability exists in this build.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Not a motion measurement — a static property-configuration fact about a Roblox `Tool` instance.
failure_modes: leaving `CanCollide` true on a held tool, causing it to physically shove or catch on other players/geometry while held or swung
leaving `Massless` false, letting a large tool part meaningfully affect the holding character's own physics (fall speed, balance) simply by being equipped

skipping the Grip Editor step and accepting wherever the part's own pivot happens to place it in the hand, producing an awkwardly-held weapon needing a manual rotate/offset fix after the fact (the source's own account: 'doesn't look the best just yet... let me just rotate it a bit')
roblox_considerations: This entire entry is Roblox-engine-specific: `Tool`, `Handle`, `CanCollide`, `Massless` and the Grip transform are all native Roblox concepts with no equivalent outside it.
performance_implications: `Massless=true` avoids unnecessary physics simulation cost from a held part that need not affect the character's own mass/momentum.
examples: a unioned sword part renamed 'Handle', set `CanCollide=false` and `Massless=true` explicitly and directly (video @ 02:15–02:26)

the Tool Grip Editor plugin used to set the exact hand grip position and a 90° rotation correction after the default grip looked wrong (video @ 02:51–03:48, confirmed in this session's own frame at t=03:29 showing the Tool Grip Editor panel open)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/I1T5Rcm9g3E @ 02:15–03:48 — Nobel Courses (the presenter) demonstrates every step directly on screen, naming each property explicitly; UI confirmed in this session's own frame at t=03:29; experimental until validated
